column1: # Project Gutenberg: 50 English books, a standard corpus of EPUBLib (doc/testing.md, "Corpus runs").
# Fetch with scripts/fetch-corpora.sh, which verifies each book against its sha256 here. Agents may
# fetch it: the files come only by the routes Project Gutenberg's robot-access policy
# (https://www.gutenberg.org/policy/robot_access.html) names, the offline catalog and the mirror its
# robot/harvest endpoint links to. That mirror is aleph.gutenberg.org, whose certificate names
# aleph.pglaf.org. Each file is the EPUB 3 "with images" build. Gutenberg rebuilds these files
# monthly at the same URL, so a mismatch means re-pinning.
# Selection, 2026-10-14, from the RDF offline catalog
#   candidates are English texts (type Text, sole language en) with an EPUB 3 "with images" file,
#   not in "Category: Encyclopedias/Dictionaries/Reference", ranked by the catalog's download
#   count (most first, ties by number). Genre from the "Category:" bookshelves: drama =
#   Plays/Films/Dramas; poetry = Poetry, not drama; shorts = Short Stories, not drama or poetry;
#   novel = Novels, or an LCSH subject containing "fiction"; nonfiction = the rest.
#   1. long (4): the 3 largest plain-text files among the 48 most downloaded candidates, and the
#      largest among the 48 most downloaded nonfiction candidates;
#   2. novel (16), shorts (8), poetry (7), drama (7), nonfiction (8): each genre in download order.
#   Every step skips a book already chosen.
# Columns: url, sha256, bytes, title, genre, number (the Gutenberg ebook number).
